title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Accounting earnings can be sculpted by a single tax ruling or inventory build; ten-year free cash flow and return on invested capital never lie.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Principle

web_blocks.html: A 10-year review from FY2017 to FY2026 shows Qualcomm's full cycle. FY2017–FY2020 brought flat sales and legal fines, including a -$4.96B GAAP net loss in FY2018 [17, 18]. Next came the FY2021–FY2022 5G boom, lifting sales to $44.20B and operating income to $15.86B [17]. An inventory glut hit FY2023 ($35.82B sales) before diversification lifted FY2026 revenue back to $43.12B [17, 18].

web_blocks.caption: Table 6.1: Qualcomm 10-Year Financial Forensics (FY2017–FY2026, $ Billions)
web_blocks.takeaway: Qualcomm doubled sales from $22.3B to $43.1B over ten years and earned ~$76.2B in total FCF. FY2026 FCF-to-Net-Income fell to 63% due to a $4.21B tax benefit and a $2.11B inventory build.

web_blocks.html: Forensic readers should look past FY2026's headline net income jump. GAAP Net Income rose to $13.63 billion even though operating income fell 30% from $12.36 billion to $8.66 billion [2, 3]. That gap came from an $11.3 billion tax swing. In FY2025, Qualcomm booked a $7.12 billion tax expense [3]. In FY2026, it booked a $4.21 billion discrete tax benefit [2, 3]. Stripping out that one-time tax gain and $3.45 billion in Stock-Based Compensation puts true economic Free Cash Flow near $5.2 billion [3].

Balance-sheet health as of September 27, 2026 stays investment-grade. Liquidity dipped slightly after $6,806 million in buybacks, $2,868 million in dividends, and the Alphawave deal [3, 16]. Cash and marketable securities totaled $7,681 million ($4,636M cash plus $3,045M securities), down from $10,155 million in FY2025 [1, 3]. Restricted cash also fell from $2,323 million to $0 [3]. Debt stood at $15,112 million in notes ($2,492M short-term, $12,620M long-term; ~$15.99B broader debt), leaving ~$7.43 billion in net debt [1, 3, 17]. Equity was $30,401 million on $60,829 million of assets, with a 1.86x current ratio and 1.12x quick ratio [3].

web_blocks.caption: Table 6.2: Capital Return, SBC Dilution & Return on Capital Forensics (FY2025–FY2026)
rows: Exceptionally high vs. ~9%–10% WACC, powered by asset-light QTL & fabless QCT [Blind Snapshot].
28.5% payout ratio; 5.3% 3Y / 6.4% 5Y dividend CAGR [3, Blind Snapshot].
Significant non-cash expense; ~51% of $6.8B buybacks merely offset SBC dilution [3].
Net share count shrinking ~2.5%–3% annually after SBC offset [2, 3].
web_blocks.takeaway: Qualcomm's 31.1% ROIC beats its cost of capital by over 20 points. Still, investors must deduct $3.45B in Stock-Based Compensation (8.0% of sales), which absorbs half of annual buybacks.

web_blocks.mechanism: Leveraged fabless-era semiconductor complexity and high-ROIC installed-base services to dampen hardware cyclicality, while returning >90% of Free Cash Flow via buybacks and dividends.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Compounded revenue from $9.7B (FY15) to >$27B (FY24–25) while shrinking diluted share count by ~30% and sustaining >25% ROIC across two memory/logic downturns.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: High-ROIC semiconductor franchises that pair cyclical hardware with recurring IP or service streams can compound per-share FCF steadily across cycles—provided buybacks do not mask rising SBC or over-lever during peak inventory builds.

book_paragraphs: When you and I pull back the camera to look at ten full years of Qualcomm's audited financials, from fiscal 2017 through fiscal 2026, two things jump off the page immediately. First, this business has doubled in scale—from $22.3 billion in revenue to $43.1 billion—while generating roughly $76 billion in cumulative Free Cash Flow without owning a single wafer fab. Second, it is unmistakably cyclical. Look at the rhythm: the 2018 regulatory and Apple storm pushed operating margins down to 2.7% and produced a $4.96 billion GAAP net loss; the 2022 5G super-cycle propelled operating income to a record $15.86 billion at a 35.9% margin; the 2023 smartphone inventory glut knocked operating income in half to $7.79 billion; and fiscal 2026 sits at $8.66 billion in GAAP operating profit while the business digests Apple's modem exit and invests heavily for data centers.

Why did fiscal 2026 GAAP Net Income jump to $13.63 billion even while operating income fell 30% from $12.36 billion to $8.66 billion? That is exactly why we do forensic accounting instead of reading headline EPS. In FY2025, Qualcomm recorded a $7.12 billion income tax expense; in FY2026, it recorded a $4.21 billion income tax benefit—an $11.3 billion swing on the tax line alone. Meanwhile, cash flow from operations fell from $14.01 billion to $11.15 billion because inventory swelled by $2.11 billion, and capital expenditures more than doubled to $2.49 billion. Free Cash Flow landed at $8.65 billion—still a healthy 20.1% of sales, just without the artificial glow of the tax benefit.

Turn to the balance sheet and you see a fortress that is slightly leaner than a year ago, yet still very comfortable. Qualcomm ended September 2026 with $7.68 billion in cash and marketable securities against $15.11 billion in notes ($15.99 billion on broader debt measures), or roughly $7.4 billion in net debt—less than one year of Free Cash Flow. Return on Invested Capital sits at 31.1%, clearing a ~9% to 10% cost of capital by more than twenty percentage points.

There is, however, one forensic line item you should never gloss over: Stock-Based Compensation. In fiscal 2026, Qualcomm paid out $3.45 billion in SBC—8% of revenue—while spending $6.81 billion on share buybacks and $2.87 billion on dividends. Put simply, Qualcomm returned $9.67 billion to shareholders—slightly more than its $8.65 billion in Free Cash Flow—and roughly half of those buybacks merely mopped up employee stock grants. Net share count is still shrinking toward 1.07 billion shares, which is constructive, but true economic Free Cash Flow after SBC is closer to $5.2 billion than $8.65 billion. Keeping that distinction sharp will serve us well when we eventually step out of the price-blind room and put a price tag on the business.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Qualcomm's 31.1% ROIC and ~$76B in 10-year FCF confirm an elite asset-light franchise, but FY2026's $4.21B tax benefit and $3.45B SBC remind us to underwrite on normalized, SBC-adjusted Free Cash Flow rather than headline GAAP net income.
